title: Canonical trivialization of absolute Frobenius pullback
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme in characteristic $p>0$. On its
small pro-etale site, the
derived pullback
along absolute $p$-power Frobenius $F_X$ has a canonical
trivialization $LF_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$. It commutes with
restriction to open subschemes and with its multiplicative iterates.
(Source for the input: [Stacks,
Tag 0F6W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F6W), label `lemma-relative-frobenius-weakly-etale` – for a weakly etale $U\to X$ the relative
Frobenius $F_{U/X}:U\to U\times_{X,F_X}X$ is an isomorphism; the
trivialization of the derived pullback and its compatibilities with
restriction and with the iterates are the content of the proof below.)

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text: Use the bounded-object small pro-etale site of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], or compatible small skeletons in its larger universe. For an object $v:V\to X$ set $u(V)=V\times_{X,F_X}X$, with structural map the second projection. It is an object of the same site by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. The Frobenius formula of [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] gives $vF_V=F_Xv$: on sections both maps send $s$ to $v^\sharp(s)^p$. Thus the fibre-product property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives an $X$-morphism $r_V=(F_V,v):V\to u(V)$. For an $X$-morphism $a:V\to W$, the two projections of $u(a)r_V$ and $r_Wa$ are respectively $aF_V=F_Wa$ and $v$, so these morphisms agree. In particular $r$ is a natural transformation from the identity to $u$. Here $u$ is the base-change functor $u_{F_X}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; its chosen fibre product $X\times_{F_X,X,v}V$ (structural map the first projection, arrows $\mathrm{id}_X\times_Xa$) is written above with its factors interchanged, through the unique isomorphism respecting the two projections. In that order $r_V$ is $(v,F_V)$, and all formulas below are transported along this isomorphism, which is natural in $V$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1; naturality calculation in paragraph 4

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-relative-frobenius-universal-homeomorphism] to the morphism $v:V\to X$ constructed in step 1. Its $r_{V/X}$ is exactly $r_V$, by the two projection equations. Consequently $r_V$ is integral and a universal homeomorphism. This input applies to every site object: no finite-type or finiteness assumption on its Frobenius is needed.

source.place: Tag 0CCB, lemma-relative-frobenius; input cited in the proof of Tag 0F6W, lemma-relative-frobenius-weakly-etale

proof.text: Both $V\to X$ and $u(V)\to X$ are weakly etale by step 1. Apply [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects] to their $X$-morphism $r_V$ to see that it is weakly etale. Together with step 2, [lem-trf-weakly-etale-homeomorphism] makes $r_V$ an isomorphism. Hence the natural transformation $r:\operatorname{id}\to u$ is a natural isomorphism. For a covering family, the squares given by $r$ identify its image under $u$ with the original family via isomorphisms, so the covering is preserved.

By [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], $(F_{X*}\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(u(V))$. Restriction along $r_V$ therefore gives a natural isomorphism $\delta_{\mathcal G,V}=\mathcal G(r_V):\mathcal G(u(V))\to\mathcal G(V)$, with inverse $\mathcal G(r_V^{-1})$. Naturality in $V$ follows from $u(a)r_V=r_Wa$, and naturality in $\mathcal G$ follows from the natural-transformation condition for a sheaf map. Thus $\delta:F_{X*}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves. The actual sheaf adjunction $F_X^{-1}\dashv F_{X*}$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]: its continuity hypothesis holds because precomposition by $u\simeq\operatorname{id}$ sends every sheaf to an isomorphic sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $(L_1,R_1)=(F_X^{-1},F_{X*})$, $(L_2,R_2)=(\operatorname{id},\operatorname{id})$, and right-adjoint isomorphism $\delta^{-1}$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\tau:F_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$, characterized by $F_{X*}(\tau_{\mathcal F})\eta_{\mathcal F}=\delta_{\mathcal F}^{-1}$. Explicitly, in the colimit of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the pair $(U,r_U)$ is terminal in $\mathcal I_U^{\mathrm{op}}$: for $(V,\phi)$ the unique arrow from $(U,r_U)$ to $(V,\phi)$ in $\mathcal I_U$ is $r_V^{-1}\phi:U\to V$, by naturality of $r$. Thus the colimit identifies with $\mathcal F(U)$ by $[x\in\mathcal F(V),\phi]\mapsto\mathcal F(r_V^{-1}\phi)(x)$, with inverse the coprojection at $(U,r_U)$. These maps commute with restrictions; sheafification leaves this sheaf unchanged. The colimit unit sends $x\in\mathcal F(V)$ to $[x,\operatorname{id}_{u(V)}]$, which this formula sends to $\mathcal F(r_V^{-1})(x)$. It therefore satisfies the displayed unit equation and is precisely $\tau$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, the section maps and taking left adjoints; Sites Tag 00WX and Categories Tag 0B65

proof.text: This is an isomorphism of the site inverse image itself. In particular fix any commutative coefficient ring $A$ and its constant sheaf $A_X$. The ring map $\rho_A:A_X\to F_{X*}A_X$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is $\delta_{A_X}^{-1}$: both send each constant section $a$ to the same constant section on $u(V)$, so uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] makes them equal. Their adjunct is therefore $c_A=\tau_{A_X}:F_X^{-1}A_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$, by the unit equation of step 4. The product comparison for the inverse image is the one induced by its identification with the identity: its two projections become the two projections of the identity functor. Naturality of $\tau$ for the action map $A_X\times\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$ now says $\tau_{\mathcal M}(r m)=\tau_{A_X}(r)\tau_{\mathcal M}(m)$. Hence $\tau_{\mathcal M}$ is linear after the coefficient action is transported through $c_A$, and it identifies the module pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] with the identity on $A_X$-modules. That node states that this pullback is exact and that its ordinary derived functor is obtained termwise. Apply $\tau$ in each degree of a complex; naturality makes it commute with differentials. The resulting natural isomorphism descends uniquely to the localization at quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2), proving $LF_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$ on $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. More generally the same argument works for any sheaf of commutative rings with the coefficient identification induced by $\tau$, since the action-map calculation does not use constancy.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, exact pullback and the maps on complexes; ordinary ringed-site operation of def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations

proof.text: Let $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ be an open subscheme. By [lem-weil-absolute-frobenius-well-defined](iv), $F_X$ restricts to $F_W$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], restriction to $W$ is restriction to the slice site over $W$, with the same covering families and coefficient sheaves. On an object $V\to W$, the base change along $F_W$ identifies with the base change along $F_X$, since $F_X^{-1}(W)=W$. The relative maps have the same two projections $(F_V,v)$, so are the same under this identification. Therefore the section map $\mathcal G(r_V)$ is unchanged by restriction. The adjoint unit equation uniquely determines its inverse-image comparison, so the same is true of $\tau$; its degreewise derived comparison is unchanged as well. More explicitly, the canonical comparison from the inverse image on $W$ to the restriction of the inverse image on $X$ sends a colimit representative $(V\to W,\phi,x)$ to the same representative with $V$ regarded over $X$. Both section maps then send it to $\mathcal F(r_V^{-1}\phi)(x)$, by step 4. The sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends this equality, giving the claimed equality for the canonical restriction comparison, rather than just an unspecified isomorphism of functors.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, restriction to an open; relative-Frobenius formulas of Stacks Tag 0F6W

proof.text:
For $b\geq0$ put $u_b(V)=V\times_{X,F_X^b}X$ and $r_V^{(b)}=(F_V^b,v)$, with $u_0\simeq\operatorname{id}$ and $r^{(0)}=\operatorname{id}$. Under the canonical identification $u_bu_a(V)\simeq u_{a+b}(V)$, the composite $u_b(r_V^{(a)})r_V^{(b)}$ has projections $F_V^aF_V^b=F_V^{a+b}$ and $v$. Thus it equals $r_V^{(a+b)}$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The powers here are exactly those of [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Induction starting with $b=0,1$ makes every $r^{(b)}$ invertible. Applying a contravariant sheaf to this displayed equality gives the composite law for $\delta^{(a+b)}$. To check the inverse-image comparison explicitly, a nested colimit representative for $(F_X^a)^{-1}(F_X^b)^{-1}\mathcal F(U)$ consists of $\phi:U\to u_a(V)$, $\psi:V\to u_b(W)$, and $x\in\mathcal F(W)$. The canonical composition comparison identifies its index with $u_a(\psi)\phi:U\to u_au_b(W)\simeq u_{a+b}(W)$. Naturality of $r^{(a)}$ and the displayed iterate equality (with $a,b$ interchanged) give
$$
 (r_W^{(a+b)})^{-1}u_a(\psi)\phi=(r_W^{(b)})^{-1}\psi(r_V^{(a)})^{-1}\phi.
$$
Consequently both the direct trivialization and the successive trivializations send this representative to $\mathcal F((r_W^{(b)})^{-1}\psi(r_V^{(a)})^{-1}\phi)(x)$. The sheafification property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends the equality to the inverse-image sheaves. Their coefficient maps also agree: on constant sections every map fixes $a\in A$, and the same sheafification uniqueness proves equality on $A_X$. Thus this is an equality of module pullback comparisons. For an arbitrary complex $K$, choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Now [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies its canonical derived composition comparison on $P$ with exactly the termwise module comparison just checked, and says the first pullback of $P$ is again K-flat with flat terms. The two proposed derived trivializations therefore agree on $Q(P)$. Naturality along the isomorphism $Q(P)\to Q(K)$ gives equality on $Q(K)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](3) gives equality of natural transformations. Hence, writing $c_{a,b}:L(F_X^{a+b})^*\to L(F_X^a)^*L(F_X^b)^*$ for that comparison, $\tau^{(a+b)}=\tau^{(a)}\circ L(F_X^a)^*(\tau^{(b)})\circ c_{a,b}$. In particular the $p^b$-power trivialization is the $b$-fold composite of the $p$-power trivialization, with the identity at $b=0$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme in characteristic $p>0$. On its
small pro-etale site, the
derived pullback
along absolute $p$-power Frobenius $F_X$ has a canonical
trivialization $LF_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$. It commutes with
restriction to open subschemes and with its multiplicative iterates.

proof.text:
An object $v:V\to X$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] is weakly
etale. Its relative Frobenius is

$$
r_V=(F_V,v):V\longrightarrow V\times_{X,F_X}X.
$$

It is integral and universally bijective. For an affine ring map
$R\to B$, the corresponding map
$B\otimes_{R,F_R}R\to B$ sends $b\otimes a$ to $b^pv(a)$.
Every $b\in B$ satisfies the monic equation $T^p-b^p=0$ over the
image, proving integrality. For an algebraically closed field
$\Omega$, a homomorphism from the tensor product to $\Omega$
specifies maps $\beta:B\to\Omega$, $\alpha:R\to\Omega$ satisfying
$\beta(v(a))=\alpha(a)^p$. The unique lift to $B$ is
$b\mapsto\beta(b)^{1/p}$: it is a ring map and its restriction to
$R$ is $\alpha$. This proves universal bijectivity. The argument
is local on $X$ and $V$, so $r_V$ is a universal homeomorphism.

Its source and target are weakly etale over $X$; the target is a
base change of $v$. Thus [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects]
shows that $r_V$ is weakly etale. For clarity, the geometric
factorization behind this Mathlib result is as follows. If
$f:U\to W$ is a map between weakly etale $X$-schemes, its graph
$\Gamma_f:U\to U\times_XW$ is the base change of
$\Delta_{W/X}$ along
$(f\circ\operatorname{pr}_U,\operatorname{pr}_W)$, so is flat.
The projection $U\times_XW\to W$ is flat as a base change of
$U\to X$. Their composite $f$ is flat. Moreover the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}&U\\
{\scriptstyle\Delta_f}\downarrow&&
\downarrow{\scriptstyle\Delta_{U/X}}\\
U\times_WU&\longrightarrow&U\times_XU
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian: on a test scheme a point of its fiber product is
$(u,(u_1,u_2))$ with $(u,u)=(u_1,u_2)$, hence is uniquely
$(u,(u,u))$. Therefore $\Delta_f$ is flat as well. These are
exactly the flatness conditions in
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].
Applying [lem-trf-weakly-etale-homeomorphism] now makes
$r_V$ an isomorphism.

The $r_V$ commute with all morphisms of site objects. Consequently
the base-change functor $V\mapsto V\times_{X,F_X}X$ is naturally
isomorphic to the identity and preserves its coverings. On sheaves,
the inverses of the restriction maps along $r_V$ give
$\mathcal F(V)\simeq(F_{X*}\mathcal F)(V)$. Taking left adjoints
gives $F_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$. Both functors are exact,
so the same maps on complexes give the derived assertion with
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Restricting the maps
$r_V$ to an open gives the same relative Frobenius there.
Composing them gives relative $p^m$-power Frobenius, proving the
restriction and iteration assertions.
